summary.overview: The project declares strong execution and validation mechanisms — package scripts, a path-filtered eval gate, per-platform CI, and a deliberate structured-log debug route — but the highest-confidence web core reaches its merge entrypoint without any repo-owned compile, type, lint, or widget-behavior check wired to it, one incident runbook still contradicts shipped code, and the bounded learning review could not reach a recurrence decision.

dimensions.label: Task Understanding
dimensions.summary: Session episodes retain the request and its corrections, but authoritative context is contested: an incident runbook disagrees with shipped code, and a duplicated plugin name leaves capability provenance ambiguous. No project-declared core boundary exists; the reviewed core map is inferred.

dimensions.label: Controlled Execution
dimensions.summary: Setup, run, and debug routes are declared in project manifests with discoverable local log sinks, and the runtime debug path is unusually deliberate. Execution was not exercised during this read-only review, and one configured protection hook is defined but not enabled in the inspected clone.

dimensions.label: Change Validation
dimensions.summary: Mechanisms exist — a hermetic CI eval job and a widget validator script — but none is wired to the merge trigger for the edits they cover: no repo workflow runs the TypeScript toolchain, the widget validator runs only by hand, and the send-path failure line drops the id that diagnostic correlation depends on.

dimensions.label: Reliable Delivery
dimensions.summary: One PR-triggered eval gate is path-scoped to the core and well-designed, but the live-behavior half of it goes neutral when the external origin is unreachable, and the acceptance decision itself (branch protection, required checks) was outside the inspected boundary, so delivery acceptance remains unobserved.

dimensions.label: Learning Capture
dimensions.summary: A bounded review completed: project memory assets are present and integrity-reviewed clean at metadata level, but the session window produced a single context group with warning codes on its sources, so repeated-work and clean-window decisions were both blocked, and no supported opportunity reached a durable owner.

findings.title: Web-core changes reach the merge entrypoint without any compile, type, or lint verdict
findings.reason: Fact: the TypeScript app core is the project's highest-confidence change area, and the repo declares lint and build commands in its package manifest, yet of the 14 tracked CI workflows only two trigger on pull requests, and neither installs project dependencies or invokes the declared lint, type-check, or build route. Inference: a change that breaks compilation or types in the web core can merge while every repo-owned check stays green. Uncertainty: branch protection and required-status configuration are external to the inspected boundary, so whether any outside check fills this gap is unknown.
expectedOutput: Update the existing Workflow owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Connect the already-declared validation route to the existing pull-request entrypoint for the web core.

## Repair

- In the package manifest, confirm the exact declared names of the lint and build scripts
- Extend the pull-request-triggered workflow that is already path-filtered to the core with a job that installs dependencies from the committed lockfile and runs those declared scripts
- Reuse the existing job pattern in that workflow (setup, timeouts, concurrency group, read-only permissions); do not add new external services

## Validation

- Run the declared lint and build scripts locally and record the result
- Open a draft change that touches the core and confirm the new job appears and reports on it (pushing requires separate authorization)

## Stop rule

- If the scripts fail for pre-existing reasons, report the failures instead of wiring a red gate; the repair stays pending

findings.title: Edits to the widget compiler ship with no automatic behavior verdict while check routing points at other platforms
findings.reason: Fact: the largest recent burst of core changes landed together with a hand-written validator script for the widget compiler, and no CI workflow references it; its only declared route compiles a single file with library checks skipped and runs it manually. The project's validation-routing guidance for these changes anchors instead on Android and iOS test files that do not exercise this code. Inference: an agent editing the widget path is actively routed to the wrong platform's tests and can finish with a false sense of coverage. Uncertainty: no project statement proves this is unintentional; several sibling scripts sit equally unreferenced, which reads as a pattern rather than an isolated oversight.
expectedOutput: Update the existing Gate owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Wire the existing widget validator into automatic coverage for the code it already checks, and correct the routing that points elsewhere.

## Repair

- Run the declared widget test route from the package manifest locally and confirm it passes on the current revision
- Add a step invoking that same script to the pull-request workflow already path-filtered to the core, scoped to the widget source directory
- Where validation routing guidance names only other-platform tests for widget changes, add the widget validator as the route for this directory

## Validation

- Confirm a pull request touching the widget directory triggers the validator job (pushing requires separate authorization)
- Confirm a deliberately broken widget fixture makes the job fail, then restore it

## Stop rule

- If the script is too brittle to run unattended, report its failure modes first; do not wire an unreliable gate

findings.title: Send-path failures are logged without the request id that diagnostic exports join on
findings.reason: Fact: the user-facing error path of the turn executor emits a failure line carrying only the conversation id, while its three sibling emitters in the same file all include a request id, and the diagnostics endpoint documents that request id as the key for per-row CI gate exports; the raw provider detail is truncated and all causes collapse into one response shape. The request id is reachable at the failure site, so it is omitted rather than unavailable. Inference: for a failing row inside a multi-turn conversation, diagnosis must fall back to conversation-level scoping, losing request-level correlation exactly when the pipeline fails. Uncertainty: impact is bounded — conversation-level correlation still works.
expectedOutput: Update the existing Code owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Restore request-level correlation on the existing failure emitter without changing the client-visible error shape.

## Repair

- In the turn executor, locate the user-facing error helper and its call site where the request identity is already available from the prepared turn
- Thread the request id into the emitted failure line, matching the format already used by the sibling emitters in the same file

## Validation

- Run the package test route that asserts the system prompt and turn contract remain unchanged
- Trigger one failing send locally and confirm the emitted line carries the same request id that the diagnostics endpoint returns for that row

## Stop rule

- If the request id genuinely is not in scope at the failure site, report that finding instead of widening function signatures speculatively

findings.title: The send-path outage runbook still directs operators through a fix that already shipped
findings.reason: Fact: the tracked incident runbook for the send path declares the outage open, states no client can fix it, and describes the CI pre-flight as fooled by the old health endpoint; the health handler was rewritten after that runbook's only commit to probe the real send path, and its own comment now describes that fooled-pre-flight claim in the past tense. Git ancestry confirms the fix landed after the document, which was never revised. Inference: two tracked project files disagree about the current failure state, and an operator or agent following the runbook during the next incident is directed at already-completed remediation. Uncertainty: no session evidence shows an actual misrouting event; the contradiction itself is verified.
expectedOutput: Update the existing Runbook owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Reconcile the incident runbook with the code that is actually shipped, against its canonical sources.

## Repair

- Compare the runbook's status and remediation sections with the current health handler implementation and its commit history
- Update the runbook to record what has since shipped, what remains open, and the date each claim was verified; keep the incident chronology intact

## Validation

- Confirm every operational claim in the runbook matches the current handler behavior described in the code
- Confirm the CI pre-flight description in the runbook matches the live gate's current health-check step

## Stop rule

- If any outage claim cannot be verified from the repository alone, mark it explicitly as unverified rather than asserting resolution

findings.title: Two enabled plugins share one name, leaving it unclear which one answers the slash command
findings.reason: Fact: the asset integrity review found exactly one deterministic governance defect — two enabled plugins from two different sources carry the same canonical name, at different versions, producing a name-resolution collision over which source owns the active capability. This was verified from plugin manifest metadata, not inferred from counts. Inference: when the shared name is invoked, neither the operator nor an agent can predict which distribution supplies the behavior, and version-targeted fixes may land on the inactive copy. Uncertainty: the inspected evidence does not establish which plugin is currently active, that either is stale, or that any incorrect routing has already occurred.
expectedOutput: Update the existing Config owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Resolve the name-collision decision only at metadata level; do not edit plugin contents.

## Repair

- Use the plugin manager to list the enabled plugins and confirm which source currently wins name resolution for the colliding name
- Record the verified active source, and decide between disabling one source or renaming one, keeping removal or uninstall behind explicit confirmation

## Validation

- Re-run the asset integrity review and confirm the name-collision group is gone
- Confirm invoking the shared name reaches the source selected in the record

## Stop rule

- If the plugin manager cannot show which source is active, stop and report that gap; do not uninstall either source on inference
